tasks.gr6-shapes-t3: Topic: Properties of 2D shapes and 3D objects. Cover identifying polygons (triangle to octagon), counting sides and angles, and properties of 3D objects (faces, edges, vertices) including cubes, cylinders, cones, spheres, and pyramids. Ask Grade 6 learners to identify shapes, state properties, and distinguish 2D from 3D.
tasks.gr6-symmetry-t3: Topic: Symmetry and reflections. Cover lines of symmetry, counting lines of symmetry in shapes, reflections across vertical and horizontal axes, and identifying symmetrical figures. Ask Grade 6 learners to identify lines of symmetry, draw reflection images, and explain symmetry in shapes.
tasks.gr6-length-t3: Topic: Length and measurement. Cover units of length (millimetres, centimetres, metres, kilometres), converting between units, choosing appropriate units, and estimating lengths. Ask Grade 6 learners to convert between length units, choose sensible units, and solve length calculation problems.
tasks.gr6-area-perimeter-t3: Topic: Area and perimeter. Cover the meaning of perimeter (boundary length) and area (surface covered), formulas for rectangles and squares, and solving problems. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate perimeter and area of rectangles and squares, distinguish between area and perimeter, and apply correct units.
tasks.gr6-volume-t3: Topic: Volume of 3D objects. Cover the meaning of volume, cubic centimetres, the formula length × breadth × height, and counting unit cubes. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate volume using the formula, count unit cubes, and apply volume in practical contexts.
tasks.gr6-add-subtract-6digit-t3: Topic: Adding and subtracting whole numbers up to 6 digits, and problems. Cover estimating by rounding to the nearest 10 000 or 100 000, column addition and subtraction including borrowing across zeros, the properties of addition, compensating, and problems: summation, a missing part, increase and decrease, comparison by difference and finding the original amount. Write numbers with a space between groups of three digits (469 134) and rand amounts as R224 442. Ask Grade 6 learners to calculate and to choose the operation that a problem needs, with whole-number answers.
